messages:
Alex Kim: incident-bot just paged P-2343 — increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate from multiple regions, started ~14:05 UTC. seeing spike in token errors and timeouts. @runtime-oncall can you triage primary?
incident-bot: P-2343 created: high error rate /v1/generate, affected: hosted-api; severity: page.
runtime-oncall: I'm on it. initial check: model instances returning 502/504, KV cache hit rate dropped. grabbing logs now. tagging @infra-oncall in case networking or node pressure.
Jamal Reed: heads up — I'm still wrapping a db migration until 14:40 UTC, can be secondary if needed but limited.
Alex Kim: noted. Who's primary after the 15:00 UTC handoff? Maria?
Maria Gonzalez: I can take primary at 15:00 UTC but only if handoff is clean. @Alex please summarize current state before then.
runtime-oncall: quick triage notes:
- error pattern across replicas in us-west & eu-west
- tail logs show repeated `OOM` in backend transform service around tokenization step
- CPU and GPU utilization on model pods looks ok, but transformer workers show increasing memory allocations
- KV cache (redis) latency spiked ~14:03 UTC

infra-oncall: I'm seeing transient kube-scheduler evictions on a subset of nodes (nodepool-rt-3). disk pressure events at 14:02-14:06 UTC. No recent infra deploys.
Tess O'Neill: any customer-impact flags? support-oncall?
support-oncall: Monitoring shows ~12% of requests failing with 5xx globally, impacted customers: a handful of PLG apps with heavy streaming usage. I pinged primary contacts. prepping a status note if needed.
runtime-oncall: mitigation attempts: restarting transform workers on affected nodes, dropping cache warmers, switching routing off nodepool-rt-3. Applied temporary fallback to smaller model variant for high-latency requests.
Alex Kim: good. Add a sticky note: runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/5xx-generator — follow Runbook > Step 2 (drain nodes) then Step 4 (model fallback).
Maria Gonzalez: I'm going to join the call at 14:20 UTC. Can someone post the quick command to check eviction events?
infra-oncall: command I used: ```kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Evicted -A --since=10m``` also check node pressure: ```kubectl describe node nodepool-rt-3-xyz```
Jamal Reed: small ask — we have a coverage gap 14:40–15:00 UTC where I'm unavailable. Maria taking primary at 15:00 covers most but we need secondary from 14:40. @Tess can you cover 14:40–15:20?
Tess O'Neill: I can take secondary 14:40–15:20. will keep notifications on.
security-oncall: quick security check — no anomalous IAM activity correlating with the timestamps. logs show only normal service accounts. will keep watching.
runtime-oncall: mitigation status update 14:18 UTC: restarted 6 transform pods, KV latency recovered partially after redis node failover, fallback model reduced error rate by ~7%. still seeing errors ~6%.
support-oncall: I'll draft a customer-facing blurb: "Some customers may see transient 5xx on /v1/generate; we're actively mitigating and will provide updates." ping me edits.
Alex Kim: Good. Action items: 1) infra to validate disk pressure root cause (infra-oncall) 2) runtime to continue restarts and monitor model fallback effectiveness 3) security monitors 4) support prepare comms. Everyone acknowledge.
infra-oncall: ack — investigating ephemeral disk pressure, checking daemonset logs, will escalate if nodepool issues persist.
runtime-oncall: ack — will keep rollback plan ready and prepare canary for restoring full model.
security-oncall: ack.
support-oncall: ack, posting comms in #support-updates now.
Maria Gonzalez: joining call now. Alex — quick summary for handoff at 15:00: what would you like me to watch specifically?
Alex Kim: watch error rate, KV hit rate, and model fallback ratio. I also left a note in the runbook about checking `transform_worker_errors` metric and threshold 5/min. If error rate > 5% re-enable autoscale for transform workers to 3x for 10m.
Maria Gonzalez: got it. Also we should decide cross-team routing for future: runtime handles model-level issues and fallbacks, infra handles node/cluster capacity and cloud infra, security only for anomalies, support for customer comms. Can we stick that into the incident template?
Tess O'Neill: yes, let's add a short routing matrix to the incident runbook. I'll open a PR.
Jamal Reed: small compliance note — if fallback model changes output shape we need to notify customers in the comms. support-oncall, please check for schema changes.
support-oncall: will validate and flag any API contract changes.
runtime-oncall: update 14:32 UTC: error rate down to ~3.1% after scaling transform workers + redis failover. continuing to monitor for 15m.
incident-bot: P-2343 severity downgraded to small-impact at 14:35 UTC after mitigations.
Alex Kim: thanks all. Handoff plan: I'm primary until 15:00 UTC, Maria primary 15:00–22:00 UTC, Tess secondary 14:40–15:20 UTC, Jamal limited secondary until 14:40. If anything spikes between 14:40–15:00, page both Maria and Tess.
Maria Gonzalez: noted, will take over. leaving final checklist in thread before 15:00.
Tess O'Neill: will monitor alerts and handle paging for that window.
runtime-oncall: closing loop: will run post-incident summary and include metrics graphs (latency, 5xx rate, redis latency, node evictions).
Alex Kim: thanks — let's reconvene in #postmortems if root cause confirmed.
Maria Gonzalez: ack, thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
